headline: OSISKO METALS RELEASES 2.15 BILLION TONNE GASPÉ COPPER MRE — 0.37% CuEq Confirms One of North America's Largest Undeveloped Copper Projects
snippet: Osisko Metals (TSX: OM) announced a November 23 updated Mineral Resource Estimate for the Gaspé Copper Project in Quebec, reporting 2.15 billion tonnes in measured and indicated categories grading 0.37% copper equivalent — confirming Gaspé as one of the largest undeveloped copper deposits in North America. The update incorporates results from the 50,000-metre drill program that began in spring 2026, upgrading inferred tonnes accumulated since the April MRE. At current copper prices and with North American supply gaps widening amid AI datacenter build-out, a Tier 1-scale undeveloped deposit in a Tier 1 Quebec jurisdiction is precisely what institutional copper buyers are struggling to find.

headline: COLLECTIVE MINING EXPANDS APOLLO PIT SHELL 60M IN ALL DIRECTIONS — 146m at 1.07 g/t AuEq Opens New Open-Pit Growth at Colombia's Largest Porphyry Discovery
snippet: Collective Mining (NYSE/TSX: CNL) reported 146.10 metres grading 1.07 g/t AuEq from the Apollo Shallow Halo Zone in Colombia, with the intercept extending up to 60 metres beyond the existing Mineral Resource boundary — indicating the current pit shell understates the deposit. Fifteen of seventeen holes in the latest batch cut intervals above open-pit cut-off grade. The result arrives as the company approaches its fully-funded 20,000-metre 2026 drill target and plans the first NI 43-101 resource estimate, expected mid-2027. A Northern Miner analyst quoted in coverage noted 'results suggest the pit shell understates the shallow halo zone,' setting up a resource estimate that could surprise to the upside.

headline: FOX TUNGSTEN CUTS 3.1M AT 2.29% WO3 AND 5.3M AT 1.92% WO3 AT RC SOUTH — BC Program Hits 97% of 20,000m Target With 51 Holes Still Assaying
snippet: Fox Tungsten (TSX-V: FOXT) reported high-grade tungsten intercepts at the RC South zone of its BC project — 3.1 metres at 2.29% WO3 and 5.3 metres at 1.92% WO3 — as the company reaches 97% of its 20,000-metre 2026 drill target with 51 holes still awaiting assay results. With China named as the sole source for over 85% of global refined tungsten output and no significant North American mine in production, high-grade BC tungsten results carry supply-security implications beyond their standalone economics. The pending 51-hole batch means this program has not yet told its full story.

headline: NEXCEL CONFIRMS VISIBLE COARSE WOLFRAMITE IN HOLE BH26-05 — New Brunswick Tungsten Project Hits Critical Mineral as Drilling Advances West
snippet: Nexcel Metals (CSE: NEXX) reported that diamond hole BH26-05 at the Burnt Hill Tungsten Project in New Brunswick intersected visible coarse-grained wolframite in quartz veins, with drilling advancing to test a western extension of the deposit. Visible mineralogy ahead of assays is a qualitative confirmation that the drill program is testing the right structures. Burnt Hill is one of Canada's few active tungsten exploration programs, with zero domestic Canadian tungsten production and 85%+ global supply concentrated in China — placing critical mineral status on any North American tungsten discovery of meaningful grade.

headline: YUKON SILVER DISCOVERY EXPANDS 100M SOUTHWEST AT HALDANE — Silver North Awaits 16 More Drill Holes to Define Full Extent of Keno Hill Discovery
snippet: Silver North Resources (TSX-V: SNAG) extended the Main Fault mineralization at the Haldane silver project in Yukon's Keno Hill district approximately 100 metres southwest, with hole HLD24-30 intersecting 1.83 metres grading 1,088 g/t silver. The company completed its largest drilling program to date — 24 holes totalling 6,169 metres — with 16 holes still pending assay results. Silver at $43/oz represents a 60% discount from its 2026 high, making high-grade undeveloped ounces in a Tier 1 Yukon district among the sector's most undervalued assets on a resource-dollar basis.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $3,640 ON THANKSGIVING-THIN VOLUME — PCE Print Wednesday Is Season's Final Make-or-Break Catalyst Before Year-End
snippet: JM Bullion's November 24 market preview documents gold consolidating near $3,638 as Thanksgiving-shortened trading windows begin compressing volumes and markets hold position ahead of Wednesday's PCE release. Silver holds near $43.55/oz after Monday's recovery. With US markets closed Thursday and running a half-day Friday, the PCE print is the last liquid macro catalyst of November — a hot read revives near-certainty of a December 50bps hike and could unwind this week's recovery in thin holiday-week conditions. Wednesday's window is effectively the only remaining full-liquidity opportunity to price the Fed's December trajectory.

headline: JUNIOR EXPLORERS PIVOT TO PRIVATE EQUITY AS PUBLIC MARKETS STAY SHUT — Retail and Institutional Capital Drying Up for Grassroots Exploration
snippet: MiningIR's November 19 analysis documents the accelerating shift among junior explorers toward private equity and strategic investor capital as retail and institutional flows for early-stage exploration remain near multi-year lows. The structural consequence: grassroots exploration that generates tomorrow's mines is increasingly funded by concentrated, return-focused capital rather than broad retail participation — creating both a valuation floor problem for existing juniors and a discovery deficit risk for the decade ahead. For self-directed retail investors on TSX-V, the piece identifies deal structures that signal genuine strategic conviction versus opportunistic bridge financing.

headline: JEFFERIES BUILDS GOLD MINER POSITIONS AS GDXJ HITS 4-YEAR OVERSOLD EXTREME — Investment Bank Accumulating Into Retail Capitulation
snippet: VBL GoldFix's November 23 market commentary covers Jefferies' decision to build positions in gold mining equities as the GDXJ junior gold miner ETF reached its most oversold reading in four years following the 9% weekly correction. The piece contextualizes the institutional move as a contrarian signal distinct from retail capitulation: investment bank accumulation into forced selling has historically preceded sustainable rallies, though the author flags Wednesday's PCE as a circuit-breaker — a hot read could reset the thesis with a fresh round of hawkish repricing. The key distinction Jefferies makes: miners at current prices offer mid-2022 valuations against earnings near all-time highs.

headline: CAPITAL MARKETS THAWING FOR MINE DEVELOPERS — CRUX: Strategic Equity Replacing Expensive Private Equity as Project Finance Returns
snippet: Crux Investor identifies a selective capital markets recovery for development-stage mining projects, with Agnico Eagle's C$57 million investment in Radisson Mining Resources as a leading indicator of strategic equity returning to the sector. Traditional project debt and royalty structures are replacing expensive private equity and streaming deals, with developer valuations versus project net asset values at historic extremes. The analysis explicitly contrasts this developer-stage thaw with the continued freeze in grassroots exploration capital — suggesting a bifurcated recovery is more likely than a rising tide that lifts all juniors.

headline: US CONGRESS LABELS CHINA'S LATIN AMERICA MINING PUSH 'NEOCOLONIAL' — Bipartisan Report Flags Chilean Copper, Argentine Lithium, Brazilian REEs
snippet: A bipartisan US congressional report documented by BNAmericas calls China's investment pattern across Chilean copper, Argentine lithium and Brazilian rare earth projects a 'neocolonial' structure designed to control strategic mineral flows rather than develop host economies — recommending accelerated US engagement in Latin American mining corridors. The report identifies specific projects where Chinese state-linked capital has acquired controlling positions across all three countries. For junior miners operating in the region, the finding creates near-term risk and longer-term opportunity: increased US strategic attention means financing, permitting and offtake partnerships tied to allied-nation supply chains could add a premium to otherwise discounted projects.

headline: GOLD MINERS: RSI FOR THE SECTOR BREAKS SUB-30 — Only 2 Names Below Oversold Threshold, Signaling Selective Not Broad Capitulation
snippet: An Investing.com technical analysis finds only two gold mining companies — Gold Reserve and Contango Silver & Gold — with RSI readings below the conventional 30 oversold threshold, despite the sector's 9% weekly gold price drop and 16-19% ETF drawdown. The screen's takeaway: the correction has not yet produced sector-wide capitulation; recovery potential is concentrated in names with balance sheet resilience rather than simply the cheapest stocks. The analysis provides a framework for distinguishing distressed names from fundamentally discounted ones — a critical distinction when margin-call selling creates uniform drawdowns regardless of company quality.
